Git branching is a powerful feature of version control that helps teams work together without conflicts. Instead of everyone editing the same code directly, developers create *feature branches*—separate copies of the project where they can safely add new features or fix bugs. This keeps the main branch stable and clean.

Once a feature is finished, the developer opens a *pull request*, which is a formal request to merge the branch back into the main codebase. Team members can review the changes, leave comments, and test the code before approving it. After approval, the branch is merged, and the new work becomes part of the project. This simple workflow—branch, review, merge—ensures that everyone stays aligned and that mistakes are caught early, making collaboration smoother and more reliable.
